entries.name:
guideline: Keyboard focus.

Thumbnails can be navigated usi

fields.before: Thumbnails display a preview of an image, layer, or effect, and appear in a variety of locations as a visual reference.
fields.after:
Keyboard focus.

Thumbnails can be navigated using a keyboard in certain scenarios, such as layers or layer masks. When a thumbnail is used as pure representation of an item, focus should be set on the component the thumbnail is used within.

fields.before: Thumbnail sizes scale exponentially. The opacity checkerboard responsively resizes to appropriately fit within each thumbnail size.
fields.after:
Image.

Thumbnails feature rounded corners and may include images with transparency. A subtle inset border helps distinguish images that might otherwise blend into the product's theme colors.

guideline: Layer.

When thumbnails are used in layer manage

fields.before: Thumbnails can be navigated using a keyboard in certain scenarios, such as layers or layer masks. When a thumbnail is used as pure representation of an item, focus should be set on the component the thumbnail is used within.
fields.after:
Layer.

When thumbnails are used in layer management (such as Treeview, Compact or Detail Layers panels), the thumbnail is given a thick gray border.

When a user selects a thumbnail

fields.before: Thumbnails feature rounded corners and may include images with transparency. A subtle inset border helps distinguish images that might otherwise blend into the product’s theme colors.
fields.after:
Selected layer.

When a user selects a thumbnail in layer management, such as in Treeview, Compact or Detail Layers panels, it is highlighted with a thick blue border.

entries.name:
guideline: Using thumbnails in treeview.

Tree view items c

fields.before: When thumbnails are used in layer management (such as Treeview, Compact or Detail Layers panels), the thumbnail is given a thick gray border.
fields.after:
Using thumbnails in treeview.

Tree view items can show thumbnails as an alternative to icons. Thumbnails are best used when a user needs to have a preview of the content represented by the tree view item. Icons can be used as a fallback for when an image is unavailable, but should be appropriately sized to match the thumbnail.

entries.name:
guideline: Be mindful of thumbnail size and proportions.

T

fields.before: When a user selects a thumbnail in layer management, such as in Treeview, Compact or Detail Layers panels, it is highlighted with a thick blue border.
fields.after:
Be mindful of thumbnail size and proportions.

Tree views with thumbnails should use a thumbnail size that is appropriate to the size of the tree view itself. For example, an extra-large tree view would not work well with small thumbnails; those proportions may be better suited for using icons instead.

Icons can be used as a fallback for when an image is unavailable, but should be appropriately sized to match the thumbnail.
fields.after:
Multiple thumbnail.

In some cases, multiple thumbnails need to be displayed in-line with the tree view item (e.g., layer masks). These thumbnails should be individually selectable and inherit all other behaviors of a standard tree view item, such as drag-and-drop behavior. Don't use more than 3 thumbnails per tree view item.

source.title: feat(design-data): anatomy review A0 for accordion, field-label, thumbnail and opacity-checkerboard

fields.before: Figma S2 Web thumbnail page; SWC gen2 Thumbnail.ts:16 and thumbnail.css:24 draw the checkerboard behind transparent images. border removed as container styling (thumbnail.css:37-42); square renamed to opacity-checkerboard and relationship scope.part repointed.
fields.after: Figma S2 Web thumbnail page; SWC gen2 Thumbnail.ts:16 and thumbnail.css:24 draw the checkerboard behind transparent images. No anatomy change. border is container styling (thumbnail.css:37-42), not a part: the recipe draws it on container, over the children. opacity-checkerboard is a nested recipe at size s that fills the container; its colors and tile size come from the opacity-checkerboard component. The Figma checkerboard tile is 4px; on mobile the nested tile is 5px (see the source-conflict bead under spectrum-design-data-5m92.5.1).
